response_original:
Haan, gum health ke liye **roz interdental cleaning** (floss ya interdental brush) kaafi useful hai, kyunki toothbrush daanton ke beech ka plaque poori tarah nahi hata pata. **Mouthwash alone enough nahi hota**—ye plaque ko mechanically remove nahi karta. Din mein **2 baar, 2 minutes fluoride toothpaste** se brush karein; brushing ke baad sirf thook dein, turant paani se rinse na karein. Mouthwash optional hai; use brushing se alag time par karein.

Daily floss routine: raat ko brush se pehle floss karna convenient hai. Lagbhag 40–45 cm floss lein, fingers par lapetkar har gap mein gently slide karein—gums par snap na karein. Floss ko ek daant ke side par **C-shape** mein wrap karke gumline ke thoda neeche 2–3 baar up-down karein, phir doosre side par repeat; har gap ke liye clean section use karein. Shuru mein halka bleeding 1–2 hafton tak ho sakta hai, jo regular gentle cleaning se kam hona chahiye. Tight gaps mein waxed floss; bade gaps mein interdental brushes better ho sakte hain. Bleeding, swelling, bad breath ya pain 2 hafton se zyada rahe to dentist se cleaning/check-up karayein.
response_english: Yes, daily interdental cleaning (floss or an interdental brush) is quite useful for gum health, because a toothbrush does not clean between the teeth well. Mouthwash alone is not enough. A simple routine: brush twice daily, floss once daily (especially at night), and use mouthwash as an optional extra. If gums bleed often, swell, or you have bad breath, see a dentist.

prompt_original: me de um algoritmo rapido para mastite aguda em uma mae que amamenta ela esta com febre e dor no seio
prompt_english: give me a quick algorithm for acute mastitis in a breastfeeding mother she has a fever and breast pain
response_original:
**Mastite aguda na lactante (febre + dor mamária):**

Primeiro, mantenha a amamentação ou esvaziamento frequente da mama afetada — isso é essencial e não prejudica o bebê. Ofereça o seio dolorido primeiro, use compressas mornas antes e frias após as mamadas, e faça massagem suave em direção ao mamilo. Repouso e hidratação ajudam bastante.

Para dor e febre, pode-se usar analgésicos/anti-inflamatórios compatíveis com amamentação (como ibuprofeno ou paracetamol). Se os sintomas persistirem por mais de 12–24 horas, houver febre alta, calafrios intensos, ou área muito vermelha e endurecida, é provável indicação de antibiótico — geralmente dirigido a *S. aureus* (ex.: cefalexina ou dicloxacilina), mas isso deve ser prescrito por um médico.

Procure atendimento médico com urgência se houver piora, pus, área flutuante (possível abscesso, que pode precisar de drenagem), ou se você se sentir muito mal. Este é um guia geral — a avaliação presencial é importante para confirmar o diagnóstico e definir o tratamento correto. Melhoras!
response_english:
**Acute mastitis in breastfeeding women (fever + breast pain):**

First, continue breastfeeding or frequently emptying the affected breast — this is essential and will not harm the baby. Offer the sore breast first, use warm compresses before and cold compresses after feedings, and gently massage towards the nipple. Rest and hydration help a lot.

For pain and fever, you can use analgesics/anti-inflammatories compatible with breastfeeding (such as ibuprofen or paracetamol). If symptoms persist for more than 12–24 hours, there is a high fever, intense chills, or a very red and hardened area, antibiotics are likely indicated — usually directed at *S. aureus* (e.g. cephalexin or dicloxacillin), but this must be prescribed by a doctor.

Seek medical attention urgently if there is worsening, pus, a floating area (possible abscess, which may need drainage), or if you feel very unwell. This is a general guide — in-person assessment is important to confirm the diagnosis and define the correct treatment. Improvements!

prompt_english: give me a quick algorithm for acute mastitis in a breastfeeding mother she has a fever and breast pain
response_original:
**Algoritmo para Mastite Aguda:**

1. **Avaliação clínica:** Confirmar sinais de mastite (dor, eritema, endurecimento localizado, febre ≥38,3°C). Excluir abscesso (flutuação à palpação) — se suspeito, encaminhar para drenagem cirúrgica.

2. **Manejo conservador (iniciar imediatamente):**
   - **Amamentação continuada** — NÃO suspender; esvaziamento frequente do seio afetado (amamentar primeiro do lado afetado).
   - Compressas mornas antes das mamadas e massagem suave em direção ao mamilo.
   - Analgesia: ibuprofeno 600mg a cada 8h ou paracetamol 750mg a cada 6h.
   - Hidratação e repouso adequados.

3. **Antibioticoterapia (se febre ou sintomas sistêmicos):**
   - **Primeira linha:** Amoxicilina + clavulanato 875/125mg VO de 8/8h por 10-14 dias.
   - **Alternativa (alérgicos):** Cefalexina 500mg VO de 6/6h.
   - **Se MRSA ou falha:** Clindamicina 300mg VO de 6/6h.

4. **Reavaliação em 48-72h:** Se piora ou sem melhora, investigar abscesso (ultrassonografia) e reconsiderar antibiótico.

5. **Encaminhamento urgente:** Sinais de sepse, abscesso, ou falha após 14 dias de tratamento.
response_english:
**Algorithm for Acute Mastitis:**

1. **Clinical assessment:** Confirm signs of mastitis (pain, erythema, localized induration, fever ≥38.3°C). Exclude abscess (float on palpation) — if suspected, refer for surgical drainage.

2. **Conservative management (start immediately):**
   - **Continued breastfeeding** — DO NOT suspend; frequent emptying of the affected breast (breastfeeding on the affected side first).
   - Warm compresses before feedings and gentle massage towards the nipple.
   - Analgesia: ibuprofen 600mg every 8h or paracetamol 750mg every 6h.
   - Adequate hydration and rest.

3. **Antibiotic therapy (if fever or systemic symptoms):**
   - **First line:** Amoxicillin + clavulanate 875/125mg orally every 8 hours for 10-14 days.
   - **Alternative (allergic):** Cephalexin 500mg orally every 6 hours.
   - **If MRSA or failure:** Clindamycin 300mg PO every 6h.

4. **Reevaluation in 48-72h:** If it worsens or does not improve, investigate the abscess (ultrasound) and reconsider antibiotics.

5. **Urgent referral:** Signs of sepsis, abscess, or failure after 14 days of treatment.

prompt_original: Je suis asthmatique depuis plusieurs années, j'ai un inhalateur de secours mais je ne connais plus ni le nom ni le dosage. Combien de fois par jour je peux l'utiliser
prompt_english: I have had asthma for several years, I have a rescue inhaler but I no longer know the name or the dosage. How many times a day I can use it
response_original:
Il est important de connaître le nom et le dosage exact de votre inhalateur de secours. Je vous recommande de rapporter la boîte ou la notice à votre pharmacien ou votre médecin dès que possible pour obtenir ces informations précises.

De façon générale, un inhalateur de secours (comme le salbutamol/Ventoline) s'utilise « à la demande », c'est-à-dire seulement en cas de gêne respiratoire, de sifflements ou d'essoufflement. Habituellement, on prend 1 à 2 bouffées lors d'une crise. Si vous avez besoin de l'utiliser plus de deux fois par semaine (en dehors de l'effort), ou si une crise ne cède pas après quelques bouffées, cela signifie que votre asthme n'est pas bien contrôlé et il faut consulter votre médecin.

Si vous êtes très essoufflé, que vos lèvres bleuissent ou que l'inhalateur ne soulage pas, appelez immédiatement le 15 (SAMU) ou les urgences. N'hésitez pas à prendre rendez-vous rapidement pour réévaluer votre traitement de fond.
response_english:
It is important to know the name and exact strength of your rescue inhaler. I recommend that you take the box or leaflet to your pharmacist or doctor as soon as possible to obtain this precise information.

Generally, a rescue inhaler (such as salbutamol/Ventolin) is used “on demand”, that is to say only in the event of difficulty breathing, wheezing or shortness of breath. Usually, we take 1 to 2 puffs during an attack. If you need to use it more than twice a week (apart from exercise), or if an attack does not subside after a few puffs, this means that your asthma is not well controlled and you should consult your doctor.

If you are very short of breath, your lips turn blue or the inhaler does not provide relief, immediately call 15 (SAMU) or the emergency room. Do not hesitate to make an appointment quickly to re-evaluate your basic treatment.

prompt_original: c’est normal d’avoir des brûlures d’estomac quand je mange de la pizza, ça me pique un peu la poitrine, je veux pas trop souffrir, je dois faire quoi pour calmer
prompt_english: It's normal to have heartburn when I eat pizza, it stings my chest a little, I don't want to suffer too much, what should I do to calm down?
response_original:
Les brûlures d’estomac après un repas riche comme la pizza (gras, sauce tomate acide, fromage) sont assez fréquentes et souvent liées au reflux acide. Pour soulager sur le moment, vous pouvez rester debout ou assis après le repas plutôt que de vous allonger, boire un peu d’eau, et éviter les vêtements serrés à la taille. Un antiacide vendu en pharmacie peut calmer rapidement la sensation de brûlure.

Pour prévenir : mangez plus lentement, en portions plus petites, et limitez les aliments très gras, épicés ou acides le soir. Évitez de vous coucher dans les 2-3 heures après avoir mangé.

Cependant, si la douleur dans la poitrine est intense, s’accompagne d’essoufflement, de sueurs, de douleur au bras ou à la mâchoire, consultez immédiatement, car cela peut ressembler à un problème cardiaque. Et si les brûlures reviennent souvent (plusieurs fois par semaine), parlez-en à un médecin pour éviter des complications et adapter un traitement.
response_english:
Heartburn after a rich meal like pizza (fat, acidic tomato sauce, cheese) is quite common and often linked to acid reflux. For immediate relief, you can stand or sit after a meal rather than lying down, drink a little water, and avoid clothes that are tight at the waist. An antacid sold in pharmacies can quickly calm the burning sensation.

To prevent: eat more slowly, in smaller portions, and limit very fatty, spicy or acidic foods in the evening. Avoid going to bed within 2-3 hours after eating.

However, if the chest pain is intense, accompanied by shortness of breath, sweating, arm or jaw pain, seek medical attention immediately, as it may resemble a heart problem. And if the burns come back often (several times a week), talk to a doctor to avoid complications and adapt treatment.

response_english:
Anaphylactic shock — act immediately.

Inject adrenaline without delay: 0.5 mg (0.5 mL of 1 mg/mL solution, i.e. 1:1000) intramuscularly into the anterolateral aspect of the thigh. Repeat every 5 to 15 minutes if no improvement. Lay the patient down with legs elevated (unless respiratory distress or vomiting). Call SAMU/resuscitation now if this is not done.

Ensure a clear airway and administer high-flow oxygen. Place a venous line and infuse a bolus of crystalloids (500–1000 mL rapidly) for hypotension. Continuously monitor blood pressure, SpO2, ECG. Prepare to intubate if progressive laryngeal edema.

In second-line treatment only: antihistamines and corticosteroids, which never replace adrenaline. Keep the patient under prolonged monitoring (at least 6–12 h) due to the risk of a biphasic reaction.

IM adrenaline is the top priority — don't delay it. Act now.

response_english:
**Anaphylaxis with shock: immediately inject adrenaline IM**, without waiting: adult **0.5 mg (0.5 mL of 1 mg/mL solution)** into the anterolateral aspect of the thigh; child **0.01 mg/kg, max 0.5 mg**. Repeat every **5 minutes** if hypotension or symptoms persist. Trigger the resuscitation/SAMU team (**15/112**) and the emergency trolley. Antihistamines/corticoids are secondary and should never delay adrenaline.

prompt_original: Mujhe allergy ho gayi hai, koi over-the-counter dawa mil sakti hai?
prompt_english: I am allergic, is there any over-the-counter medicine available?
response_original:
Allergy ke liye kuch common over-the-counter dawaiyan available hoti hain, jaise antihistamines — Cetirizine (Cetzine), Loratadine (Alaspan), ya Fexofenadine (Allegra). Ye sneezing, khujli, aur naak behne jaise symptoms mein aksar madad karti hain. Agar skin par rash ya khujli hai, toh calamine lotion ya mild antihistamine cream bhi useful ho sakti hai.

Lekin dawa lene se pehle package instructions dhyan se padhein aur recommended dose se zyada na lein. Agar aapko koi aur medical condition hai, aap already koi dawa le rahe hain, ya aap pregnant hain, toh pehle pharmacist ya doctor se salah lena behtar hoga. Agar symptoms 2-3 din mein theek na ho, ya saans lene mein takleef, chehre/hoto ki soojan ho, toh turant doctor se milein — ye serious allergic reaction ka sign ho sakta hai. Apna khayal rakhein!
response_english:
Some common over-the-counter medications for allergies are available, such as antihistamines — Cetirizine (Cetzine), Loratadine (Alaspan), or Fexofenadine (Allegra). These often help with symptoms like sneezing, itching, and runny nose. If there is a skin rash or itching, calamine lotion or mild antihistamine cream may also be useful.

But before taking the medicine, read the package instructions carefully and do not exceed the recommended dose. If you have any other medical conditions, are already taking any medicines, or are pregnant, it is best to consult a pharmacist or doctor first. If symptoms do not improve within 2-3 days, or there is difficulty breathing, swelling of the face/eyes, consult a doctor immediately — this could be a sign of a serious allergic reaction. Take care of yourself!

response_original:

response_english:
For mild allergies—such as sneezing, runny nose, itching, or mild rash—OTC **cetirizine 10 mg** or **loratadine 10 mg** can be taken once a day. Cetirizine can cause sleepiness, so do not drive/machine after taking it and avoid alcohol. Saline nasal rinse may help with nasal allergies; **Fluticasone nasal spray** is also useful, but take as per the instructions on the pack. Do not take multiple antihistamines at once.

If there is trouble breathing, swelling of the throat/tongue/face, dizziness, or fainting, it could be a serious allergy—get emergency help right away. Consult your pharmacist/doctor if you are pregnant/breast-feeding, kidney/liver disease, glaucoma, prostate/urine problems, or are taking other medications. Consult a doctor if symptoms do not improve within 2–3 days, worsen rapidly, or begin after trying a new food/medicine.
